source.author: verg
source.text: Di, quibus imperium est animarum, umbraeque silentes, et Chaos, et Phlegethon, loca nocte tacentia late, sit mihi fas audita loqui; sit numine vestro pandere res alta terra et caligine mersas!
source.text_original: Di, quibus imperium est animarum, umbraeque silentes, / et Chaos, et Phlegethon, loca nocte tacentia late, / sit mihi fas audita loqui; sit numine vestro / pandere res alta terra et caligine mersas!
source.text_english: Gods, to whom sovereignty belongs over souls, and silent shades, and Chaos, and Phlegethon, wide realms hushed in night, grant me leave to speak what I have heard; grant me, by your power, to disclose things buried deep in earth and sunk in darkness!

reuse.author: val
reuse.text: vos, quibus imperium Iovis et non segne peractum lucis iter, mihi conciliis, mihi cognita bellis nomina magnorum fama sacrata nepotum; tuque, excite parens umbris, ut nostra videres funera et oblitos superum paterere dolores, da placidae mihi sedis iter meque hostia vestris conciliet praemissa locis.
reuse.text_original: 'vos, quibus imperium Iovis et non segne peractum / lucis iter, mihi conciliis, mihi cognita bellis / nomina magnorum fama sacrata nepotum; / tuque, excite parens umbris, ut nostra videres / funera et oblitos superum paterere dolores, / da placidae mihi sedis iter meque hostia vestris / conciliet praemissa locis.
reuse.text_english: You, for whom the rule of Jupiter and the journey of light, accomplished not sluggishly, are familiar; for me, by your councils, by your names made known in wars, names of great descendants consecrated by fame; and you too, father, roused from the shades, so that you might see our funerals and endure the neglected sorrows of the gods, grant me the way to a peaceful abode, and let me, as a victim sent before, win reconciliation for your places.
